title: What is exception handling in C#?

data.text: **Question:** What is exception handling in C#?

Exception handling in C# uses try-catch-finally blocks to handle runtime errors. The try block contains code that might throw, catch blocks handle specific exceptions, and finally runs cleanup code regardless of exceptions.

**try block:** Contains code that might throw an exception.

**catch block:** Handles specific exception types. Can have multiple catch blocks for different exceptions.

**finally block:** Runs regardless of whether an exception occurred. Used for cleanup like closing files or connections.

**throw:** Used to raise exceptions. Use throw; to preserve stack trace, throw ex; loses it.

data.title: Exception Handling

data.caption: If an exception matches a catch block it is handled; otherwise it propagates up. finally always runs.
